Method of Attack: Asking users to provide fingerprint to access app features but instead popping up a subscription screen that automatically charges a saved credit card for $99 to $119 USD
Using fake reviews to appear legitimate and beneficial
Charging users automatically if Touch ID is enabled and credit card is saved
Discoverer: ESET mobile app security researcher Lukas Stefanko
Impacted Systems: iPhone X (partially protected with Double Click to Pay)
older iPhone models with Touch ID enabled
Attack Vector: Malicious iOS fitness apps requesting fingerprint authentication
Indicators of Compromise: Fake 5-star reviews and automated developer responses on Reddit
